title: Sleeping Area
preview: On the second floor, the windmill becomes intimate. This was not only a working building, but also a place where the miller's family rested beside the stored wheat and flour.
details: Please watch your step on the wooden stairs and mind the low timber above you. The windmill was built for work first, so every movement inside it asks for attention.

On one side, historic images show windmills from across Greece. On the other, the room recalls a more personal truth: the miller and his family slept close to the sound, movement and responsibility of the mill.
Bags of raw wheat and fresh flour were stored nearby. Keeping them close was practical and protective, because flour was food, income and security for the household.
This floor shows how closely work and private life could meet in an island family. Rest, storage and responsibility shared the same small space.
Continue upward to the machinery, where the wooden structure and stone wheels reveal how wind became flour.

items.text: Listen for the sounds around you and imagine sleeping while the wind moved the sails.
Find where wheat and flour could be kept close to the family.
